processing: Fully oxidised Ceylon black tea, with a reputation for its small Dust 1 grade.
harvest_season: Year-round. Dimbula teas are generally most prized from the dry months early in the year.
appearance_dry: Dark, fine broken leaf or dust, by grade.
appearance_liquor: Bright reddish-amber, as is typical of Dimbula.
appearance_wet: Small coppery-brown particles in the fine grades.
taste_profile: Few notes exist for the estate alone. As with other Dimbula teas, expect a brisk, clean, full cup with a light floral edge.

brewing.notes: Western style. Dust grades infuse in moments, so keep them short, and use a fine filter.

vintage_note: Sold by estate and grade at the Colombo auction, with no vintage year, and much of it goes into trade channels. Buy recent production, and for classic Dimbula character look to early-year lots, as with neighbouring estates.
description:
Mattakelle is a Dimbula estate in Nuwara Eliya District, 9 km from Talawakelle town, at about 1,372 m and covering around 362 hectares. Talawakelle Tea Estates PLC, part of the Hayleys Group, manages it.

The unusual thing is what it is known for: Dust 1, a grade many drinkers overlook. In auction reports the estate has repeatedly set records with it, including Rs. 1,200 per kg in the Western High Grown category in January 2022.

Dust brews fast and strong. As with other Dimbula teas, expect a brisk, clean cup, and keep the steep short or it turns harsh.

This is mainly a trade tea, so a retail pack under its name is uncommon. If you find one, the grade tells you more than the estate name does.
history: Little is documented about when the estate was founded or who first owned it. What shows up on record is its modern life: management under Talawakelle Tea Estates PLC and a run of auction records, from a first-ever Rs. 1,000 for its Dust 1 to the 2022 figure.
